title: ديوان الإمام الشافعي
author: محمد بن إدريس الشافعي
publication_date: Collected posthumously, most modern editions 20th-21st century
edition_analyzed: Most common Arabic edition, widely circulated in the Arab world
target_audience: Students of Islamic studies and Arabic literature
Seekers of wisdom and ethical guidance
primary_purpose: To convey moral wisdom, religious reflection, and practical advice through eloquent poetry, drawing from both personal experience and profound Islamic teachings.

structure_format.narrative_style: Rhymed and metered classical Arabic poetry, often didactic and aphoristic
structure_format.organization: A collection of short poems (often two to eight lines each), organized by subject or theme in most printed editions
features: Frequent allusions to Qur'anic and Prophetic teachings

key_concepts_lessons: Necessity for humility and shunning arrogance
Transience of worldly life and goods
Importance of sincere intention in deeds
Virtue of silence and guarding one's speech
Nobility of forgiveness and overlooking faults
Seeking knowledge as a lifelong pursuit
Reliance on God and acceptance of His decree
notable_features: Attributed to a towering figure of Islamic jurisprudence and intellectual history
Widely memorized and quoted in the Arabic-speaking and Islamic world
Frequent adaptation into proverbs and maxims
Combines scholarly insight with poetic artistry
cultural_historical_context: Imam al-Shafi'i was the founder of the Shafi'i school of Islamic law and a major figure in early Islamic intellectual history. The diwan was compiled from poetry attributed to him, expressing his ethical, spiritual, and philosophical perspectives—widely admired for both their literary and moral value. While some poems' attribution is debated, the collection reflects central values of classical Arabic and Islamic culture.
reception_impact: Highly respected in scholarly, religious, and literary circles
Used in religious sermons and educational settings
Source of inspiration for generations of readers
Some poems widely memorized as aphorisms
Scholarly debates on authenticity of particular pieces
comparable_titles: ديوان الإمام علي (The Diwan of Imam Ali)
الزهد والرقائق لابن المبارك (Kitab al-Zuhd by Ibn al-Mubarak)
حكم ابن عطاء الله السكندري (The Hikam of Ibn Ata'illah al-Sakandari)
ديوان الحسن البصري (Diwan of Hasan al-Basri)
